issue.title: Capture sase-1ez live after-measurement and 24h soak on a TUI restarted onto the landed code

task_type_fields.proposal:
Run the live before/after acceptance capture for epic sase-1ez (plan:202610/tui_freeze_gc_heap.md, phase `acceptance`) once the user's ACE TUI runs the landed code. The capture must include the sase-1ez closeout tale's config-token revalidator fix, and the TUI has to be restarted by the user, not by an agent (tui_perf.md rule 15).

1. Confirm the TUI has restarted onto landed code. `~/.sase/logs/tui_startup.jsonl` rows should carry `app_instance_id`, and `tui_stalls.jsonl` should contain `tui_gc_pause` / `tui_memory_heartbeat` rows. As of 2026-10-02 22:27 EDT there were none: the newest startup row (19:52) predates the telemetry. If no such rows exist, ask the user through /sase_questions to restart the TUI.
2. On one `app_instance_id` starting ≥20 min after the restart, run `tools/tui_freeze_report` over a busy hour, then over a 4-hour RSS window. Use /sase_monitor to wait out the windows.
3. Compare against the baselines: 10.7-12.9% frozen by the watchdog (sase-1ez.8 reproduced 12.31% over 478 s, median 2.5 s, on the old log); gen-2 at 16.7% and all GC at 25.5% of wall time; gen-2 p50 2.16 s; RSS 1.48 -> 4.66 GB plus 1.46 GB swap in 50 min.
4. Targets: zero automatic or backstop gen-2 collections starting within 2 s of input; idle-collection p95 ≤ 500 ms; total GC < 3% of wall time; < 0.5% of wall time in hitches, with no `late` hitches except idle-collection ones; RSS growth < 0.5 GB over 4 h with VmSwap about 0; j/k p95 < 16 ms (`SASE_TUI_PERF=1` or tests/ace/tui/bench_tui_jk.py).
5. Also run a 24-hour soak on the same instance, as sase-1ez.8 note #3 proposed.
6. Record a before/after table plus an evidence artifact. File each miss through /sase_new_task. A miss on idle collections or RSS makes the deferred LinkIndex-into-sase_core follow-up from the plan's Out of scope section worth reconsidering.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Proposed by sase-1ez.8 (notes #1 and #3). This cannot be part of the sase-1ez landing. It needs the user to restart their TUI onto code that includes the landing tale's own commit, followed by multi-hour capture windows (busy hour, 4 h RSS, 24 h soak). The epic closeout must not wait on that commit or those windows. The code, telemetry, and report tool (tools/tui_freeze_report) it uses have all landed and are verified by tests.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1ez's acceptance phase (sase-1ez.8 notes #1 and #3) could only reproduce the before-baseline: the live TUI never restarted onto the telemetry, so the after-measurement and soak remain as follow-up verification.
